content.text:
I submitted **index 50** (Ca 0.17, Cu 0.23, V 0.60). It had the highest EQE of the three compositions I measured, at **1.76%**. I don't know how that compares with the best composition in the library.

The budget allowed only 3 merit measurements:

| Index | Composition (Ca / Cu / V) | EQE |
|---|---|---|
| 139 | 0.22 / 0.54 / 0.24, Cu-rich | 0.47% |
| 44 | 0.19 / 0.14 / 0.67, V-rich | 1.41% |
| 50 | 0.17 / 0.23 / 0.60, V-rich | **1.76%** |

- **Trend:** EQE was much higher in the V-rich part of the library than in the Cu-rich part. Among the V-rich points, it went up as the Cu:V ratio moved toward about 1:2 (the ratio of the copper vanadate CuV₂O₆) and Ca went down. Three points is a small sample, so this is a rough guide rather than an established trend.
- **Why I skipped the model's pick:** the Gaussian-process model suggested index 37 for exploration. Its predicted EQE there (about 0.6%) was below what I had already measured, so I used the last measurement on index 50 instead.
- **Not used:** I made no XRD measurements (5 were available), so no phase identification backs this result. The list of known crystal structures was too large to return, and I didn't read the saved copy.

The most likely place to look for something better is nearby V-rich compositions with lower Ca, such as indices 31 and 51. None of them have been measured.
